OD-B01-S02#3.speaker: Athena
OD-B01-S02#3.caption: And I go to Ithaca myself, to breathe strength into his son. I will set Telemachus on his feet, send him to call the Achaeans to assembly, and then across the sea to Pylos and Sparta for news of his father, so the boy may win a name among men.

OD-B01-S02#5.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B01-S02#5.caption: Athena fastens the gold sandals, closes her hand around the spear, and drops from Olympus.

OD-B01-S03#3.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B01-S03#3.caption: Telemachus sees the unattended stranger and crosses the hall, ashamed of his own house.

OD-B01-S03#5.speaker: Telemachus
OD-B01-S03#5.caption: Welcome, stranger. You are kindly come to our house; give me your spear. Eat first, and afterward tell me what you need, but come, away from this noise.

OD-B05-S04#2.speaker: Calypso
OD-B05-S04#2.caption: Here at the island's edge the tall trees stand — alder and poplar and sky-high fir, long dry, that will ride light on the water. Take the great bronze axe and the adze; here is cloth for a sail and cord to lace her. Build, and I will bring all the rest.

OD-B05-S04#3.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B05-S04#3.caption: Calypso fells, trims, bores, joins, decks, and fences the timbers over four days.

OD-B05-S04#5.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B05-S04#5.caption: Calypso bathes and clothes him, loads food and water, and sends a warm wind behind the raft.

OD-B09-S08#3.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B09-S08#3.caption: Odysseus selects a green olive trunk, cuts and smooths it into a stake, and hardens its point in the fire.

OD-B09-S08#6.speaker: Odysseus
OD-B09-S08#6.caption: Here, Cyclops — drink wine on that man-flesh you have eaten, and learn what drink our ship carried. You ask my name, and I will tell it for the guest-gift you promised: Nobody is my name. Nobody — so my father and mother and all my friends call me.

OD-B09-S09#2.speaker: Polyphemus
OD-B09-S09#2.caption: Give me more, freely — and here is your gift, Nobody, to warm your heart: I eat Nobody last, after all his friends. There is my guest-gift to you.

OD-B09-S09#3.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B09-S09#3.caption: Odysseus heats the stake until it glows and the chosen men drive it into the Cyclops's eye.

OD-B09-S09#5.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B09-S09#5.caption: Polyphemus wakes with a roar and tears it free.

OD-B09-S09#7.speaker: Cyclopes outside
OD-B09-S09#7.caption: What ails you, Polyphemus, that you wake the deathless night with screaming — is some man stealing your flocks, or killing you by craft or force? If Nobody harms you, alone as you are, it is sickness sent by Zeus, and cannot be helped — pray to your father Poseidon.

OD-B09-S10#2.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B09-S10#2.caption: Odysseus binds three rams abreast for each man, suspending a sailor beneath the middle animal.

OD-B09-S10#5.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B09-S10#5.caption: Outside, the men release themselves, drive the flock to the ship, and row away.

OD-B10-S01#3.speaker: Aeolus
OD-B10-S01#3.caption: Take this bag of oxhide, Odysseus — every rough wind is bound inside, sewn shut with silver wire. I loose the West Wind only; let it carry you home to Ithaca.

OD-B10-S01#4.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B10-S01#4.caption: After nine days Ithaca appears, but Odysseus falls asleep at the helm.

OD-B10-S01#5.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B10-S01#5.caption: The crew opens the bag, believing it contains treasure, and the winds blast them back to Aeolia.

OD-B10-S01#6.speaker: Aeolus
OD-B10-S01#6.caption: Out of my island — out, worst of living men! You come back cursed; the blessed gods themselves hate you. I give no help to what heaven hunts.

OD-B12-S03#2.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B12-S03#2.caption: Odysseus softens wax and seals every crewman's ears.

OD-B12-S03#3.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B12-S03#3.caption: The men bind him upright to the mast and row past the flowered shore.

OD-B12-S03#5.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B12-S03#5.caption: Odysseus struggles and signals to be released.

OD-B12-S03#6.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B12-S03#6.caption: Perimedes and Eurylochus tighten the ropes until the song fades.

OD-B12-S04#1.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B12-S04#1.caption: The crew hears Charybdis roar and sees spray rising from the whirlpool.

OD-B12-S04#3.speaker: Odysseus
OD-B12-S04#3.caption: Row, friends — we have been in worse and lived, and this too we shall remember. Helmsman, hold her off that smoke and hug the cliff — keep to the rock, or you kill us all.

OD-B12-S04#5.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B12-S04#5.caption: Scylla's six heads strike, lifting six screaming men from the ship.

OD-B12-S04#6.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B12-S04#6.caption: The survivors pass beyond both monsters while watching their companions die above them.

OD-B13-S01#5.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B13-S01#5.caption: The ship runs faster than a hawk while he sleeps and reaches Ithaca before dawn.

OD-B21-S07#1.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B21-S07#1.caption: Odysseus strings the bow effortlessly, as a musician strings a lyre.

OD-B21-S07#5.speaker: Zeus
OD-B21-S07#5.caption: It is time, son of Laertes. I have set my sign on the day.

OD-B21-S07#7.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B21-S07#7.caption: Odysseus nocks an arrow and shoots cleanly through all twelve axes.

OD-B21-S07#8.speaker: Odysseus
OD-B21-S07#8.caption: Telemachus, the stranger sitting in your hall has not disgraced you. I did not miss the mark, and the bow did not wear me out. Now it is the hour for supper, while there is still light, and after supper there is other sport in this house.

OD-B23-S04#2.speaker: Penelope
OD-B23-S04#2.caption: Eurycleia, carry the great bed out of the bridal chamber and set it up in the hall. Spread the fleeces and the bright blankets on it for him there.

OD-B23-S04#3.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B23-S04#3.caption: Odysseus erupts, explaining that he built the bed around a living olive tree and no one could move it intact.

OD-B23-S04#5.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B23-S04#5.caption: Penelope runs to him and embraces him.

OD-B23-S04#7.speaker: Penelope
OD-B23-S04#7.caption: Do not be angry with me; of all men you were always the shrewdest. I was afraid some stranger would come with a smooth story and take me with it. Now the sign has come and my heart gives way, and you are as welcome to me as dry land to swimmers.

OD-B23-S04#8.speaker: Epic Narrator
OD-B23-S04#8.caption: Athena holds back dawn while husband and wife weep and reunite.
